title: Make founder intent records one contract, require section 8 on every distant horizon, and guard intent and horizon ids against deletion through cleanup
problem: Directive 2026-10-28 section 11 asks that every material founder intention be recorded with fourteen named elements and that old statements be preserved even when superseded; section 8 asks that every capability not yet buildable keep its enabling interfaces, the conditions that would make it feasible and the conditions that would falsify it; section 54 says 'CLOSE PR does not mean DELETE THE INTENT' and 'Do not accidentally kill founder intent.' On the unit's base 44b3df96 (#236's head): 0 of the 26 docs/intent JSON records conformed to one contract (151 required-field errors against the new contract), and they used different names for the same field (state, status, lifecycle_state; intended_outcome, intended_observable_effect). None of the 31 horizons on greg/path.json that are not CURRENTLY_BUILDABLE carried enabling_interfaces, feasible_when or falsified_by, and greg.path.validate() did not ask for them. Deleting INTENT-20261014-competency-compiler.json and horizon selective_web3_settlement went unnoticed by all 52 base test files that read docs/intent or the path (2626 passed, 1 failed, a Stackelberg timing failure only).
founder_intent_refs: Founder Intent Ledger, 'Required Intent Record' (15 fields) and 'The canonical ledger should ultimately become machine-readable'
baseline: 44b3df96 (#236's head, since adopted into #196 as 2161dbe2): 26 JSON intent records in docs/intent with mixed field names and no shared contract; 7 markdown intent records; a ledger that names 36 intent ids as whole tokens; greg/path.json with 40 horizons (31 not buildable) and 13 frontier backcasts; greg.path.validate() checks node, horizon and backcast fields but no section 8 element; no committed record of which intent and horizon ids exist, and no check that any of them is still present.

alternatives.name: Proposed: one contract with additive normalization, section 8 checked at load, and a typed continuity guard
alternatives.description: contracts/intent-record.schema.json (JSON Schema 2020-12) requires the ledger's 15 fields plus the 5 section 11 adds; a field a record's source does not supply carries {"unrecorded": reason}, and identity fields never can. All 26 records are normalized additively (22 fields copied from the name the same record already uses, 7 GOAL-GRAVITY fields copied from its own Intent Record document, 122 unrecorded markers, ratcheted by MAX_UNRECORDED). greg.path.validate() requires the three section 8 fields on every non-buildable horizon, each a pointer to the horizon's own text, a verbatim value with its source, or a named gap; greg path reports the gaps. scripts/ci/check_intent_continuity.py checks HEAD against a committed snapshot of 122 ids pinned at 44b3df96; an id may leave only when a successor of its kind lists exactly that id in supersedes; a re-pin only adds. A 59-mutant gate holds all of it.
advantages: Every JSON intent record validates against one contract: 26 of 26 at the head, 0 of 26 at the base
Gaps are counted and named instead of absent: 122 record fields, 15 falsifiers and 17 enabling-interface sets
A cleanup that deletes a pinned intent or horizon fails the continuity test; it reads no git history, so shallow CI clones work
Both evidence scripts rebuild all 26 records and greg/path.json byte for byte from a git archive of the base
#236's build-frontier semantics are unchanged: build_status, achieved and the primary node are the base's
disadvantages: Edits 26 founder records and greg/path.json, which other units also read
The phrase rule cannot prove that a path-sourced phrase names an interface
The continuity check and the mutation gate are not CI steps; the check runs only through its unit test
JSON Schema cannot compare two texts, so intended_effect's agreement with its older names is test-enforced, not contract-enforced
alternatives.revival_evidence: Retained; revisit when the S11-A ledger unit validates the ledger's markdown records against the same contract.

alternatives.name: Simplest viable: contract and one validation test, records untouched, a fixed id list in a test
alternatives.description: Add the schema and a test that validates docs/intent against it; leave the records as they are; freeze the current intent and horizon ids as a list inside a test; add no section 8 check.
advantages: No edit to any founder record or to greg/path.json
Fewer lines and no evidence scripts
disadvantages: 0 of 26 base records conform, so the validation test fails on day one or must skip every record
Gaps stay invisible: a missing field and an unrecorded field look the same
A fixed list has no lawful exit for a superseded id and no re-pin rule, so it is edited away at the first legitimate change
Section 8 stays unenforced on all 31 distant horizons
alternatives.revival_evidence: If editing founder records is ruled out by the founder, the contract could ship with every record listed as non-conforming instead.

alternatives.name: Strongest competing: a machine-readable ledger with git-history deletion checks and CI wiring
alternatives.description: Convert docs/FOUNDER_INTENT_LEDGER.md and the markdown records into JSON records validated by the contract, enumerate authority_level and consequence_class, detect deletions from git history (git log --diff-filter=D), and wire every check into .github/workflows/canonical-ci.yml.
advantages: Covers the ledger's own table records and the markdown records, which this unit only guards for continuity
Enumerated authority and consequence values could be checked mechanically
Every check would run in CI
disadvantages: Edits docs/FOUNDER_INTENT_LEDGER.md, which the unit's scope forbids because of open PR #220
Edits canonical-ci.yml, which is on the unit's avoid list and is edited by open PR #214
Git history is not available on CI's shallow clones
Enumerating authority_level and consequence_class is a founder and ledger-owner decision (the S11-A unit)
alternatives.revival_evidence: When #220 and the canonical-ci.yml PRs land and the founder rules on authority and consequence values, the S11-A unit builds it on this contract.

alternatives.name: Staged / reversible experiment: report-only first, enforce later
alternatives.description: Land the contract, the section 8 report and the continuity check as warnings that never fail a test, observe for a period, then turn them into failures.
advantages: Cannot block another session's work while the rules settle
Shows how often the rules would fire
disadvantages: A warning nobody reads lets a deletion through; section 54 asks not to kill intent by accident, not to notice it later
The review round showed the first rules were bypassable; a report-only mode would have hidden that
alternatives.revival_evidence: If the guard blocks lawful work in practice (a documented lawful path refused), a warn-only mode for that path is the fallback.

do_nothing_option.expected_outcome: Records keep three names for their state and two for their intended effect; distant horizons keep no falsifier or enabling interface; a cleanup can delete an intent record or a horizon and, as measured on the base, 52 test files still pass.
advantages: No edit to founder records or the path
No new check that another session must satisfy
disadvantages: Directive sections 8, 11 and 54 stay unmet on the tree
Intent deletion through cleanup stays undetected
No machine-checkable record shape for the ledger to grow into

roles.position: The unit serves sections 8, 11 and 54 without inventing intent: every copied value is the record's own words or a verbatim source, every missing field is a named gap, and the one inferred pointer (developmental_research to P10) was removed. Two choices touch founder intent itself and belong to the founder: the succession rule lets a superseded record's file leave the tree when a successor names its id, and two section 44 sentences are counted as falsifiers.
material_concerns: Section 11 says 'Preserve old founder statements even when superseded'; the guard lets a superseded JSON record leave when a successor of its kind lists its id in supersedes (review finding MUF-R7, plausible, not changed)
122 record fields and 32 section 8 entries can be supplied only by the founder or a record's owner
docs/FOUNDER_INTENT_LEDGER.md was not edited; its own table records are guarded for continuity but not schema-validated

roles.position: Commodity and existing parts only: JSON Schema 2020-12 through the installed jsonschema, the existing greg.path.validate() entry point, a committed JSON snapshot read from git archive, and one CLI. No new store, service or authority plane. The contract is the one owner of the record shape; greg.path stays the one owner of path validation.
material_concerns: Two older tests keep their own required-field lists (tests/unit/test_founder_correction_20261030.py REQUIRED, tests/unit/test_greg_seed_genome_records.py) and do not read the contract (review finding MUF-R8, plausible, not changed)
validate() reads no repository file, so a file-sourced section 8 value is checked by the unit test, not at load
Section 8 must run after frontier backcasts are validated; the first ordering changed a test_frontier_backcasts.py message (fixed in 7dc95349)

roles.position: Two reviews of a8e40155 by separate agents of this same session broke the first version in ten confirmed ways: empty pointer lists, borrowed and cut text, prose succession across kinds, re-pin laundering, snapshot thinning, an unenforced contract, seven false gap markers and an overclaim. Each was reproduced before any change and is now refused, with regression tests that fail on a8e40155 and 20 new mutants. The residuals are stated limits, not hidden passes.
material_concerns: The phrase rule proves only that a value is the horizon's own uncut words; a fragment such as 'a running Body' still passes
Thinning the pinned ids takes a visible edit of the snapshot and the test's frozen counts and digest; a hand edit of an 'added' entry is caught only by review

Two section 44 sentences ('Revenue generated through deception is failure.', 'Engagement that destroys trust is failure.') are conduct failures, not feasibility falsifiers (review finding MUF-R6, plausible, not changed)

roles.position: Cheap to run and to undo: the three unit files take about 4 s, the continuity check reads three paths and no git history, and the evidence scripts rebuild every changed record and greg/path.json from the base. The branch merges cleanly with #196's head d35d92a5 and with 21 open or recent sibling PR heads.
material_concerns: The continuity CLI and the mutation gate are not wired into canonical-ci.yml (avoid list); the #196 integrator must add them
After #196 absorbs new intent records or horizons, someone must run --write-snapshot <commit> to protect them
Five falsifiers are copied from greg/cognition/advantage.py; a session that edits that file fails test_every_copied_value_is_verbatim_in_its_source until the copy is updated
Under container load, three unrelated timing tests failed in the 67-file run and passed alone

roles.position: Nothing is claimed beyond UNIT-TESTED and INTEGRATION-TESTED in a container. No recorded statement, state or meaning was changed; every original field keeps its value and order. Gaps are named, not filled. Negative results are kept: the base deletion went unnoticed, the first version was bypassable, and three timing tests flake under load. No person's data is touched and no authority moves.
material_concerns: The fail-before mixes kinds: some base failures are collection errors because the new modules are absent
No full-suite run: 67 related files plus repository-wide checks on the merged head
The 7 markdown intent records and intent JSON outside docs/intent (SG-001 to SG-012) are not schema-validated

pass_1.intended_outcome: A cleanup cannot delete a founder intent or capability horizon without a typed successor that names it; every founder intent record is checkable against one contract, with its missing fields named; and every distant capability carries section 8's enabling interfaces, feasibility conditions and falsifiers, or a named gap that greg path reports.

advantages.statement: One contract for every JSON intent record, with the older state names held to state
advantages.amplified_value: The S11-A ledger unit and any new record validate against the same shape; the ledger's own aim of becoming machine-readable gets a contract to grow into
The founder sees exactly which 122 fields and 32 section 8 entries only he or an owner can supply; a later record can close a gap but cannot add one without a visible edit

advantages.statement: Continuity is checked from the tree and a committed snapshot, not git history
advantages.amplified_value: Works on CI's shallow clones and in any copy of the tree; section 54 becomes a test

advantages.statement: Section 8 is a load-time invariant of the path
advantages.amplified_value: No later edit to greg/path.json can drop a distant horizon's falsifier or interfaces silently; greg path names the 15 and 17 still unrecorded

disadvantages.statement: The normalization edits 26 founder records and greg/path.json, files other units read
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Additive only and reproducible: every original field keeps its value and order, both evidence scripts rebuild the files byte for byte from the base, the Mind reconciliation map's three dispositions are corrected from kept to extended, and merge-tree is clean against the PR base and 21 sibling heads

disadvantages.statement: An unrecorded marker could hide a field the source does supply, or be read as content
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Identity fields can never be unrecorded; markers carry a reason and are counted; the ratchet blocks new ones; a test refuses a marker on a field the record's own document states (GOAL-GRAVITY's seven were found and copied)

disadvantages.statement: A section 8 pointer or value could be satisfied with text that belongs to something else, or with a fragment
disadvantages.redesigned_response: A pointer must name a field that records that element and resolve to the horizon's own text (its fields, its own frontier backcasts, a P-node it names); a path-sourced value must be an uncut phrase or name; an empty list, mixed sources and invisible text are refused

disadvantages.statement: The lawful exit (succession) and the re-pin could release ids without a real successor
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Succession is typed and whole-entry: a supersedes entry names an id only when it is that id, and only a successor of the same kind counts; a re-pin only adds and refuses while any pinned id is missing; the test freezes the pinned commit, per-kind counts and a sha256 of the pinned ids

disadvantages.statement: The continuity CLI and the mutation gate are not CI steps
disadvantages.redesigned_response: The continuity unit test runs in Canonical CI's pytest job today; adding the CLI and the gate to canonical-ci.yml is handed to the #196 integrator, since that file is on the avoid list and edited by open PRs

disadvantages.statement: The contract cannot compare texts, and markdown records and the ledger's table records are not schema-validated
disadvantages.redesigned_response: The repository test enforces intended_effect's agreement with its older names for docs/intent; the contract says so; the markdown and ledger records are guarded for continuity and left to the S11-A unit

comparisons.baseline: No contract, no section 8 fields, no continuity record: 0 of 26 records conform and a measured deletion goes unnoticed by 52 test files
comparisons.do_nothing: Sections 8, 11 and 54 stay unmet on the tree; deletion through cleanup stays undetected
comparisons.simplest_viable_alternative: Contract plus a fixed id list with records untouched: fails or skips every base record, hides gaps, and has no lawful exit for a superseded id
comparisons.strongest_competing_architecture: A machine-readable ledger with git-history checks and CI wiring: edits FOUNDER_INTENT_LEDGER.md (#220) and canonical-ci.yml (avoid list, #214), and git history is absent on shallow clones
comparisons.reversible_experiment: This change: additive, reproducible from the base by two scripts, revertible by commit, with the guard's checks removable without touching any record

rejected_alternatives.name: Detect deletions from git history

rejected_alternatives.name: Fill unrecorded fields and section 8 entries with inferred text
rejected_alternatives.rejection_reason: Inventing intent is what section 11 and the founder-effect doctrine forbid; the one inferred pointer (developmental_research to P10) was removed
rejected_alternatives.revival_evidence: The founder or a record's owner supplies the text

rejected_alternatives.name: Check file-sourced section 8 values inside greg.path.validate()
rejected_alternatives.rejection_reason: An install may ship without docs/, so validate() reads no repository file; the unit test checks file sources against their anchored section instead
rejected_alternatives.revival_evidence: A packaged copy of the cited sources ships with every install

pass_2.attack_summary: Two reviews of a8e40155 by separate agents of this same session attacked the strengthened design as deployed: pointer and value forms, ownership of cited text, succession wording, re-pin and snapshot edits, the contract's own enforcement, the truth of each gap marker, and the evidence claims. Each finding was reproduced on a git-archive copy of a8e40155 before any change. A final verification then merged the PR base d35d92a5, re-ran the gates and the related suites on the merged head e661d9c0, and checked merge-tree against the sibling PRs.

new_weaknesses.statement: Any whole-word mention of an id in any supersedes prose, across kinds, released it: 'extends INTENT-0030' and 'continuity, voice or robotics' let those ids be deleted with the CLI at exit 0 (MUF-C2, MUF-R3)

pass_2.final_design: contracts/intent-record.schema.json with 20 required fields, unrecorded markers, agreeing lifecycle names and visible text; 26 records normalized additively (22 copied fields, 7 from GOAL-GRAVITY's own document, 122 markers under a ratchet); greg.path.validate() requiring section 8's three fields on all 31 non-buildable horizons, as own-text pointers, uncut path-sourced phrases, test-checked file sources or named gaps, after backcast validation; greg path reporting the gaps; a committed snapshot of 122 ids at 44b3df96 checked by scripts/ci/check_intent_continuity.py with typed whole-entry succession and an add-only re-pin; a 59-mutant gate. No authority, activation or VEPMC change.

residual_risks.review_trigger: Any diff touching INTENT-CONTINUITY-SNAPSHOT-2026-10-30.json or the frozen digest

residual_risks.risk: The succession exit and the section 44 falsifiers may not match the founder's intent

entries.position: A superseded JSON record should not leave the tree merely because a successor lists its id; it should move to an archive path the check also reads, or its statement should be preserved in the successor (review finding MUF-R7).
entries.rationale: Section 11: 'Preserve old founder statements even when superseded.' The guard keeps the id's lineage but not the old statement's text.
entries.evidence_threshold: A founder ruling, or a superseded record deleted under the rule whose statement then exists nowhere on the tree
entries.review_trigger: The first deletion of a JSON intent record under the succession rule

entries.position: business_operation and daleobanks_media_engine should not count section 44's 'Revenue generated through deception is failure.' and 'Engagement that destroys trust is failure.' as falsifiers; they are conduct failures (review finding MUF-R6).
entries.rationale: Section 8 asks for the conditions that would falsify the capability's feasibility; counting conduct failures makes the falsifier gap 15 instead of 17.
entries.evidence_threshold: A founder ruling that these sentences are not falsifiers, or a reviewer showing they cannot falsify the capability
entries.review_trigger: Founder review of greg path's section 8 report

entries.position: The continuity CLI and the mutation gate should be Canonical CI steps, not only a unit test and a hand-run script.
entries.rationale: A gate that runs only by hand decays; CI runs the unit test but not the 59 mutants.
entries.evidence_threshold: canonical-ci.yml free of open edits, or a regression a mutant would have caught landing unnoticed

authority_impact.approver: Alfonso Lopez (adoption into #196 and any merge; rulings on MUF-R6 and MUF-R7); #196 integrator for intake

migration_plan: No runtime migration. The 26 records keep every original field, value and order, and each lists what it copied and from where in its normalization_2026_10_30 block; a consumer that reads only the older field names sees the same values. A new docs/intent record must carry the 20 fields or unrecorded markers, and a new non-buildable horizon its three section 8 fields. After #196 absorbs new intent records or horizons, run python scripts/ci/check_intent_continuity.py --write-snapshot <commit>; it appends them under 'added' and refuses if any pinned id is gone.

steps: Revert this branch's commits, or decline intake into #196
Reverting restores every record and greg/path.json to the base exactly; the evidence scripts document each inserted field
To disable only the guard, remove scripts/ci/check_intent_continuity.py, its snapshot and tests/unit/test_intent_continuity.py; no record changes

kill_criteria: Any original field of a docs/intent record changes value or order, or an added field holds text no cited source supplies
A pinned intent or horizon id is missing at HEAD while the continuity check exits 0
greg.path.load accepts a non-buildable horizon without section 8's three fields, or with an empty, borrowed or cut entry
#236's build-frontier semantics change: build_status, achieved or the primary node differ from the base on the same tree
The guard refuses a lawful path it documents (markdown record to JSON, ledger id to record, a typed successor) with no way through
decision_owner: Alfonso Lopez decides adoption into #196, the succession rule (MUF-R7), the section 44 falsifier mapping (MUF-R6) and the 122 record fields and 32 section 8 entries still unrecorded; the #196 integrator decides intake and the two CI steps; session_01Kucyfm6YBHMTjaiC1M9hqD owns the reversible draft. The Systems Architect, Adversarial Reviewer, Operator and Maintainer, and Evidence and Welfare Guardian recommend RETAIN; the Founder-Intent Steward asks for the founder's decision.
review_trigger: A founder ruling on MUF-R6 or MUF-R7; any founder or owner supplying unrecorded fields (the ratchet then lowers MAX_UNRECORDED); #196 absorbing new intent records or horizons (re-pin); canonical-ci.yml becoming free for the two CI steps; Canonical CI's first run on this PR
